title: Leviticus Chapter 27 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Leviticus chapter 27 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Leviticus Chapter 27 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Leviticus Chapter 27.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 27, what is the valuation of a male from twenty years old even unto sixty years old when a man makes a singular vow?
options: Fifty shekels of silver
Thirty shekels of silver
Twenty shekels of silver
Fifteen shekels of silver
questions.correctAnswer: Fifty shekels of silver
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:3 states that the estimation of a male from twenty years old even unto sixty years old shall be fifty shekels of silver.

questions.question: What is the valuation of a female from twenty years old even unto sixty years old when a man makes a singular vow?
options: Thirty shekels
Fifty shekels
Ten shekels
Three shekels
questions.correctAnswer: Thirty shekels
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:4 directly states that if the person is a female, the estimation shall be thirty shekels.

questions.question: In Leviticus 27, what must a poorer person do if they cannot meet the set valuation for a vow?
options: Present himself before the priest for valuation
Pay the full amount regardless
Offer a beast instead
Give a tithe of his goods
questions.correctAnswer: Present himself before the priest for valuation
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:8 explains that if he be poorer than the set estimation, he shall present himself before the priest, who will value him according to his ability.

questions.question: True or False: A man can change a vowed beast for another beast without any consequence.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:10 states that one shall not alter or change a beast; if he changes beast for beast, then both the original and the exchange shall be holy, implying it cannot be casually changed.

questions.question: What happens if a person dedicates an unclean beast that is not offered in sacrifice to the LORD?
options: The beast is presented before the priest for valuation
The beast is immediately holy and cannot be redeemed
The beast must be sacrificed
The beast must be sold to a foreigner
questions.correctAnswer: The beast is presented before the priest for valuation
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:11 instructs that if it be any unclean beast of which they do not offer a sacrifice, it shall be presented before the priest.

questions.question: True or False: The priest shall value an unclean beast, whether good or bad, as stated in Leviticus 27.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:12 clearly states that the priest shall value the beast, whether it be good or bad.

questions.question: What is the valuation for a male child from five years old even unto twenty years old when a singular vow is made?
options: Twenty shekels
Ten shekels
Five shekels
Thirty shekels
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty shekels
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:5 specifies that the estimation for a male from five years old even unto twenty years old is twenty shekels.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 27, how much is the valuation for a female child from a month old even unto five years old?
options: Three shekels of silver
Five shekels of silver
Ten shekels of silver
Thirty shekels of silver
questions.correctAnswer: Three shekels of silver
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:6 states that for a female from a month old even unto five years old, the estimation shall be three shekels of silver.

questions.question: True or False: When a man makes a vow, the persons and things vowed are considered holy unto the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:2 states that when a man makes a singular vow, the persons shall be for the LORD by estimation, meaning they are considered holy to the LORD.

questions.question: What is the valuation for a male aged sixty years old and above?
options: Fifteen shekels
Ten shekels
Twenty shekels
Five shekels
questions.correctAnswer: Fifteen shekels
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:7 states that for a male from sixty years old and above, the valuation shall be fifteen shekels.

questions.question: Which of the following comes first in the instructions of Leviticus 27?
options: The valuation of persons by age and sex
Instructions on redeeming a field
Rules about tithes
Instructions on devoted things
questions.correctAnswer: The valuation of persons by age and sex
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:2-7 first outlines the valuation of persons by age and sex before addressing fields, tithes, or devoted things later in the chapter.

questions.question: True or False: All beasts brought as an offering unto the LORD shall be considered holy according to Leviticus 27.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:9 states that all beasts given as offerings unto the LORD shall be holy.

questions.question: What must be added to the valuation if a man redeems an unclean beast that he had sanctified?
options: A fifth part of the valuation
Double the valuation
No extra amount, just the valuation
Half the valuation
questions.correctAnswer: A fifth part of the valuation
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:13 instructs that if a man redeems an unclean beast, he shall add a fifth part of the valuation unto it.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 27, can a devoted thing that a man devotes unto the LORD be sold or redeemed?
options: No, it is most holy and cannot be sold or redeemed
Yes, it can be sold or redeemed at any time
It can only be sold but not redeemed
It can only be redeemed but not sold
questions.correctAnswer: No, it is most holy and cannot be sold or redeemed
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:28 clearly states that no devoted thing shall be sold or redeemed; every devoted thing is most holy unto the LORD.

questions.question: What is the valuation for a female aged sixty years old and above?
options: Ten shekels
Fifteen shekels
Thirty shekels
Twenty shekels
questions.correctAnswer: Ten shekels
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:7 states that the valuation for a female from sixty years old and above is ten shekels.

medium.title: Leviticus Chapter 27 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Leviticus Chapter 27 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 27, what must a person add if they choose to redeem a field they have sanctified to the LORD?
options: A tenth of its estimated value
A fifth part of the money of the estimation
Double the estimated value
Nothing, it can be redeemed at the original value
questions.correctAnswer: A fifth part of the money of the estimation
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:19 states that if a person will redeem a sanctified field, they must add a fifth part of the money of the estimation. This is also consistent with similar instructions in verses 13 and 15, which require adding a fifth part when redeeming other items.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 27 say about the estimation of a field sanctified to the LORD with respect to the seed it produces?
options: The field's estimation depends on its size
The estimation is according to the seed thereof
The field is valued according to its market price
The field's worth is fixed regardless of produce
questions.correctAnswer: The estimation is according to the seed thereof
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:16 explains that when a man sanctifies part of his field to the LORD, the estimation of the field shall be according to the seed thereof, specifically valuing an homer of barley seed at fifty shekels of silver.

questions.question: If a man sanctifies his house to the LORD and later wants to redeem it, what does the law require him to do?
options: Redeem it at its original value
Add a fifth part of the estimation money to redeem it
Sell it to another person
He cannot redeem the house once sanctified
questions.correctAnswer: Add a fifth part of the estimation money to redeem it
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:15 instructs that if a man who sanctified his house wishes to redeem it, he must add a fifth part of the money of the estimation to it, reflecting the consistent rule for redemption of sanctified property seen in verses 13 and 19.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 27, what happens to a field that is sold to another man and not redeemed before the year of jubile?
options: It returns to the original owner immediately
It becomes holy unto the LORD permanently
It cannot be redeemed any more
It is given to the priest
questions.correctAnswer: It cannot be redeemed any more
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:20 states that if the owner does not redeem the field or has sold it to another man, the field shall not be redeemed anymore, emphasizing the finality of sale before the year of jubile.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 27:21 teach about the status of a field at the year of the jubile?
options: The field must be sold to the highest bidder
The field becomes holy unto the LORD and belongs to the priest
The field remains with the current owner permanently
The field is returned to the original owner without condition
questions.correctAnswer: The field becomes holy unto the LORD and belongs to the priest
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:21 declares that when a field goes out in the jubile, it becomes holy unto the LORD as a devoted field, and its possession belongs to the priest, highlighting the sacredness of land in the jubilee system.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 27 describe the priest's role when a man sanctifies a field he has bought, which is not originally his possession?
options: The priest sells the field to another buyer
The priest estimates the worth of the field until the year of jubile
The priest takes ownership of the field immediately
The priest can refuse to sanctify the field
questions.correctAnswer: The priest estimates the worth of the field until the year of jubile
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:23 explains that when a man sanctifies a field he bought, the priest shall reckon the worth of the field according to the estimation until the year of jubile, and the estimation shall be given as a holy thing unto the LORD.

questions.question: What principle about redemption and added value is taught by the passages about redeeming houses, fields, and beasts in Leviticus 27?
options: Redemption requires only the original value
Redemption is forbidden after sanctification
Redemption requires adding a fifth part to the original valuation
Redemption requires double payment
questions.correctAnswer: Redemption requires adding a fifth part to the original valuation
questions.explanation: Throughout Leviticus 27:13, 15, and 19, it is consistently stated that if one redeems a sanctified object or property, they must add a fifth part to the original estimation, reflecting the principle of added value upon redemption.

questions.question: True or False: According to Leviticus 27, if a man sanctifies a field after the year of jubile, the priest will reduce the money reckoned for that field based on the years remaining until the next jubile.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:18 states that if a field is sanctified after the jubile, the priest shall reckon the money according to the years remaining until the year of the jubile and shall abate it from the estimation, showing a proportional reduction.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 27:14 say about the priest's estimation when a man sanctifies his house to be holy unto the LORD?
options: The priest may overestimate to increase value
The priest's estimation, whether good or bad, shall stand
The owner decides the value of the house
The house cannot be sanctified
questions.correctAnswer: The priest's estimation, whether good or bad, shall stand
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:14 clearly states that when a man sanctifies his house, the priest shall estimate it, whether good or bad, and the estimation shall stand as determined, emphasizing the authority and finality of the priest's valuation.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 27 teach us about faith and trust in God through the regulation of vows and sanctification?
options: By encouraging immediate redemption without penalty
By establishing precise valuations and redemption rules to honor vows
By allowing people to alter their vows as they please
By forbidding all forms of sanctification
questions.correctAnswer: By establishing precise valuations and redemption rules to honor vows
questions.explanation: The chapter (Leviticus 27:2-34) sets clear valuations and rules about vows and sanctification, teaching believers to honor their commitments to God carefully and with integrity, reflecting faith and trust in God's holiness and justice.

questions.question: If a man sanctifies a field to the LORD from the year of jubile, what will happen to the valuation of that field according to Leviticus 27?
options: It is reduced based on years remaining
It is increased by a fifth part
It remains according to the priest's estimation
It is returned to the original owner immediately
questions.correctAnswer: It remains according to the priest's estimation
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:17 states that if a man sanctifies his field from the year of jubile, the valuation shall stand according to the estimation without abatement, unlike fields sanctified after the jubile.

questions.question: True or False: According to Leviticus 27, all devoted things, whether man, beast, or field, can be redeemed by adding a fifth part to their value.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:28-29 explains that no devoted thing, whether man, beast, or field, that is devoted to the LORD can be sold or redeemed; they are most holy and, in the case of men, must be put to death, showing redemption is not allowed for devoted things.

questions.question: What happens to the field at the year of jubile if it was bought and sanctified by a man, as described in Leviticus 27?
options: It remains with the buyer permanently
It must be sold to the priest
It returns to the original owner to whom the possession did belong
It becomes property of the king
questions.correctAnswer: It returns to the original owner to whom the possession did belong
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:24 clearly states that in the year of the jubile, the field shall return to him from whom it was bought, the original owner of the land, reinforcing the jubilee principle of land restoration.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 27 teaches that a man can change a bad beast for a good one when making an offering to the LORD without consequences.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:10 states that one shall not change a good beast for a bad, or vice versa, and if such a change is made, both the beast and the exchange become holy, implying they cannot be redeemed and must be treated as devoted to the LORD.

questions.question: How do Leviticus 27:13 and 27:19 together instruct a believer struggling with the fear of losing their sanctified property about redemption?
options: Redemption is impossible once property is sanctified
Redemption is allowed but requires adding a fifth part to the valuation
The property must be given to the priest without compensation
The owner can redeem at any price they choose
questions.correctAnswer: Redemption is allowed but requires adding a fifth part to the valuation
questions.explanation: Both verses 13 and 19 explain that if a person desires to redeem sanctified property—a beast or field—they must add a fifth part to the estimated value, offering a way to reclaim property with an added cost, teaching trust in God's provision and obedience to His rules.

hard.title: Leviticus Chapter 27 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Leviticus Chapter 27.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 27, what is the value set for a male between twenty and sixty years old when a man makes a singular vow?
options: Fifty shekels of silver
Thirty shekels of silver
Twenty shekels of silver
Fifteen shekels of silver
questions.correctAnswer: Fifty shekels of silver
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:3 states that the estimation for a male from twenty to sixty years old shall be fifty shekels of silver.

questions.question: In Leviticus 27, what must be added to the estimation if a man redeems an unclean beast he has vowed to the LORD?
options: A fifth part of the estimation
Double the estimation
Nothing is added
Half the estimation
questions.correctAnswer: A fifth part of the estimation
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:13 explains that if a man redeems an unclean beast, he shall add a fifth part of the estimation to it.

questions.question: What is the rule concerning the firstling of beasts according to Leviticus 27?
options: The firstling cannot be sanctified; it belongs to the LORD
The firstling can be redeemed with a fifth added
The firstling can be sold or redeemed
The firstling is exempt from all vows
questions.correctAnswer: The firstling cannot be sanctified; it belongs to the LORD
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:26 states that the firstling of the beasts is the LORD's and no man shall sanctify it.

questions.question: What happens to a devoted thing that a man devotes unto the LORD according to Leviticus 27?
options: It is most holy and cannot be sold or redeemed
It can be sold but not redeemed
It can be redeemed but not sold
It must be returned after a year
questions.correctAnswer: It is most holy and cannot be sold or redeemed
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:28 explains that no devoted thing shall be sold or redeemed; every devoted thing is most holy unto the LORD.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 27, what is the consequence for a man devoted to the LORD?
options: He shall surely be put to death
He may be redeemed with a fifth added
He shall be set free after a year
He shall serve the priests
questions.correctAnswer: He shall surely be put to death
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:29 states that none devoted of men shall be redeemed but shall surely be put to death.

questions.question: What is the requirement for the tithe of the land in Leviticus 27?
options: It is holy unto the LORD
It can be redeemed without adding
It must be sold to the priests
It can be exchanged for other offerings
questions.correctAnswer: It is holy unto the LORD
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:30 states that all the tithe of the land is holy unto the LORD.

questions.question: If a man wishes to redeem any of his tithes, what must he do according to Leviticus 27?
options: Add a fifth part to the value
Pay double the value
Redeem without additional payment
Offer a substitute animal
questions.correctAnswer: Add a fifth part to the value
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:31 commands that if a man will redeem any of his tithes, he shall add a fifth part thereof.

questions.question: What is the rule regarding the tithe of the herd or flock as described in Leviticus 27?
options: The tenth shall be holy unto the LORD
Only the best animals are tithed
It may be redeemed without penalty
It must be examined for defects
questions.correctAnswer: The tenth shall be holy unto the LORD
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:32 states that concerning the tithe of the herd or flock, the tenth shall be holy unto the LORD.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 27, what is forbidden regarding the tithe of the herd or flock?
options: Searching if it be good or bad or changing it
Offering a substitute animal
Redeeming it by adding a fifth
Giving it to a stranger
questions.correctAnswer: Searching if it be good or bad or changing it
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:33 explains that one shall not search whether the tithe be good or bad, nor change it; if changed, both it and the change shall be holy and not redeemed.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage similarly emphasizes the holiness and non-redeemability of devoted things as stated in Leviticus 27?
options: Numbers 18:14
Genesis 1:1
Psalm 23:1
Exodus 20:12
questions.correctAnswer: Numbers 18:14
questions.explanation: Numbers 18:14 echoes Leviticus 27:28 by stating that devoted things are most holy and belong to the LORD, emphasizing their non-redeemability.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'sanctify' in Leviticus 27, and what does it imply in the context of vows?
options: To set apart or consecrate for holy use
To cleanse from impurity
To curse or devote to destruction
To bless abundantly
questions.correctAnswer: To set apart or consecrate for holy use
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'qadash' translated as 'sanctify' means to set apart or consecrate for holy use, as seen in Leviticus 27:14, indicating the dedication of persons or property to the LORD.

questions.question: Leviticus 27 uses a specific literary device to structure the laws about vows and valuations. Which literary device is most evident?
options: Inclusio framing the chapter with declarations of the LORD’s command
Chiasm organizing valuation rules symmetrically
Parallelism contrasting male and female valuation
Metaphor comparing vows to sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio framing the chapter with declarations of the LORD’s command
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:1 and 27:34 serve as inclusio, framing the chapter by stating the LORD's command to Moses, a common literary device in Hebrew scripture to emphasize authority and completeness.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 27's teaching about the tithe connect to Malachi 3:10 in the New Testament?
options: Both affirm the tithe as holy unto the LORD and emphasize faithful giving
Leviticus forbids tithing, but Malachi commands it
Malachi describes tithes as redeemable, Leviticus does not
Neither passage mentions tithes explicitly
questions.correctAnswer: Both affirm the tithe as holy unto the LORD and emphasize faithful giving
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:30 declares the tithe is holy unto the LORD, echoed in Malachi 3:10 which calls for bringing the full tithe to the storehouse, affirming faithful giving.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 27, what is the shekel of the sanctuary composed of?
options: Twenty gerahs
Ten ounces
Thirty shekels of silver
Fifty pieces of gold
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty gerahs
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:25 explains that the shekel of the sanctuary is composed of twenty gerahs.

questions.question: True or False: According to Leviticus 27, a man can redeem a field he has sanctified after the year of jubile by paying its full price without any reduction.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:18 states that if a man sanctifies his field after the jubile, the priest shall reckon money according to the years remaining until the jubile, so the price is abated accordingly.

theological.title: Leviticus Chapter 27 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Leviticus Chapter 27 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 27:3, what is the valuation in shekels for a male between twenty and sixty years old who is vowed to the LORD?
options: Thirty shekels
Fifty shekels
Twenty shekels
Fifteen shekels
questions.correctAnswer: Fifty shekels
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:3 states that the valuation for a male from twenty years old even unto sixty years old shall be fifty shekels of silver according to the shekel of the sanctuary.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 27:8 teach about the valuation of a person who has made a vow but is poorer than the standard estimation?
options: The priest must value them according to the standard estimation
The vow is void and must be annulled
The priest shall value them according to their ability
They may substitute a beast for the vow
questions.correctAnswer: The priest shall value them according to their ability
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:8 explains that if a person is poorer than the standard valuation, he shall present himself before the priest, who shall value him according to his ability.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated by the strict valuations and regulations on vows in Leviticus 27:10?
options: God's mercy
God's justice
God's holiness
God's patience
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:10 forbids altering or exchanging vowed beasts, emphasizing that all things dedicated to the LORD are holy, revealing God's attribute of holiness requiring exactness and purity in offerings.

questions.question: In Leviticus 27:14-15, what must a person do if he wants to redeem a house he has sanctified to the LORD?
options: Add one-third of the valuation
Add the fifth part of the valuation
Offer a new sacrifice
Give the house permanently to the priest
questions.correctAnswer: Add the fifth part of the valuation
questions.explanation: Verses 14 and 15 teach that if a man sanctifies his house and then desires to redeem it, he must add a fifth part of the priest's valuation to the original amount to reclaim ownership.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 27:18-19 explain the valuation adjustment when a field is sanctified after the year of jubilee?
options: The valuation increases by the number of years remaining
The valuation is reduced according to the years remaining until jubilee
The field cannot be sanctified after jubilee
The valuation remains the same regardless of the jubilee
questions.correctAnswer: The valuation is reduced according to the years remaining until jubilee
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:18-19 states that if a field is sanctified after the jubilee, the priest shall reckon the money according to the years remaining until the jubilee, and this amount shall be deducted from the valuation.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth do Leviticus 27:26-28 reveal about things devoted to the LORD?
options: Devoted things can be redeemed for half their value
Devoted things are most holy and cannot be sold or redeemed
Only firstlings of clean beasts are redeemable
Devoted things lose their sanctity after a year
questions.correctAnswer: Devoted things are most holy and cannot be sold or redeemed
questions.explanation: Verses 26-28 teach that the firstling of beasts is the LORD's and cannot be sanctified, and that all devoted things, whether man, beast, or field, are most holy unto the LORD and must not be sold or redeemed, underscoring the doctrine of divine dedication and irrevocability of consecration.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 27:29, what is the prescribed outcome for a person devoted to the LORD?
options: They may redeem themselves by offering sacrifices
They shall be put to death without redemption
They shall be released after the jubilee year
They shall be sold as servants
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be put to death without redemption
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:29 clearly states that none devoted of men shall be redeemed but shall surely be put to death, indicating the seriousness of a vow of dedication unto the LORD.

questions.question: What theological principle about God's ownership of the land is taught by Leviticus 27:24?
options: Land ownership is permanent and unchangeable
Fields return to original owners in the year of jubilee
Fields sanctified remain with the priest forever
Land can be freely sold and redeemed at any time
questions.correctAnswer: Fields return to original owners in the year of jubilee
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:24 reveals the theological truth that land ultimately belongs to God and is only leased to His people; hence, in the year of jubilee, fields return to the original owners, emphasizing God's sovereign ownership over the land.

questions.question: How do Leviticus 27:30-31 together reveal the doctrine of tithe and redemption?
options: Tithes are optional and may be redeemed without penalty
All tithes are holy and if redeemed, require adding a fifth to the value
Tithes are only from animal herds, not crops
Tithes must be exchanged for better offerings
questions.correctAnswer: All tithes are holy and if redeemed, require adding a fifth to the value
questions.explanation: Verses 30 and 31 teach that all tithes of the land are holy unto the LORD and if a man wishes to redeem any of his tithes, he must add the fifth part of their value, showing the sanctity and required premium for redemption.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 27:32-33 teach about the nature of tithes from herds or flocks?
options: The tithe must be carefully selected and can be exchanged
The tithe is the tenth passing under the rod and must not be exchanged
Only perfect animals may be tithed
Tithes from herds may be redeemed without penalty
questions.correctAnswer: The tithe is the tenth passing under the rod and must not be exchanged
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:32-33 declare that the tithe is the tenth of whatsoever passes under the rod, and it shall not be searched for good or bad, nor changed; if changed, both the original and the change shall be holy and not redeemable.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 27:16 teach about the valuation of a field sanctified to the LORD?
options: It is based on the number of livestock
It is valued according to the quantity of seed required
It is valued by the age of the owner
It is based on the number of trees
questions.correctAnswer: It is valued according to the quantity of seed required
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:16 specifies that when a man sanctifies part of his field, the valuation shall be according to the seed thereof, with an homer of barley seed valued at fifty shekels of silver, linking valuation to agricultural productivity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially highlighted by the command in Leviticus 27:9 regarding offerings of beasts to the LORD?
options: God's justice
God's holiness
God's omniscience
God's grace
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:9 declares that all beasts brought as offerings to the LORD shall be holy, reflecting God's attribute of holiness, which demands purity and consecration in worship.

questions.question: What combined teaching about redeeming vowed property is conveyed by Leviticus 27:13 and 27:19?
options: Redeeming requires adding a tenth part
Redeeming is forbidden once a vow is made
Redeeming requires adding a fifth part to the valuation
Redeeming involves offering a substitute animal
questions.correctAnswer: Redeeming requires adding a fifth part to the valuation
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:13 and 27:19 together teach that if a person wishes to redeem a vowed beast or field, he must add a fifth part (20%) to the valuation, emphasizing the costliness of breaking a vow.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the valuation system in Leviticus 27:2-7 is arbitrary and oppressive. What does this passage actually teach about God's justice and mercy?
options: God imposes arbitrary values without consideration
Values are fixed with no room for individual circumstances
God provides standard valuations but allows adjustment based on ability
The valuations are designed to oppress the poor
questions.correctAnswer: God provides standard valuations but allows adjustment based on ability
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:2-7 sets standard valuations for vows but Leviticus 27:8 clarifies that if one is poorer, the priest shall value according to ability, showing God's justice tempered with mercy and concern for individual circumstances.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 27:22-24 illustrate the principle of divine ownership and the temporary stewardship of property in Israel’s covenant community?
options: It asserts that purchased fields are permanently owned by the buyer
It teaches that all fields are owned by the priests
It explains that fields bought may be redeemed until the jubilee, when they return to original owners
It permits unrestricted sale and redemption of land without time limits
questions.correctAnswer: It explains that fields bought may be redeemed until the jubilee, when they return to original owners
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:22-24 teaches that fields purchased are subject to redemption until the jubilee year, when they revert to the original owner, affirming the doctrine that God owns the land and people hold it as temporary stewards.
